items.headline: CERT-EU urges rapid NGINX patching after F5 discloses five unauthenticated RCE flaws
items.summary: CERT-EU Security Advisories: CERT-EU flagged F5's 18 November 2026 advisory on five NGINX vulnerabilities that let an unauthenticated remote attacker run code with worker-process privileges. Researchers have demonstrated CVE-2026-123007, but no exploitation in the wild has been reported. CERT-EU recommends patching quickly, starting with internet-facing systems. The Hacker News: CVE-2026-123007 affects NGINX's HTTP/2 support in every version since 1.9.5 (2015) and can let an unauthenticated attacker run code on servers with HTTP/2 enabled. Fixed versions 1.31.9 and 1.30.7 are available. Qualys Vulnerabilities and Threat Research: Five nginx vulnerabilities called NGINX2Root were disclosed on 18 November 2026. The lead flaw, CVE-2026-123007, is a memory corruption bug in nginx's HTTP/2 handling that F5 rates 9.2 under CVSS v4.0 and 8.1 under CVSS v3.1. An attacker without credentials can crash nginx worker processes; the source does not report exploitation in the wild.
items.importance_rationale: These are critical unauthenticated RCE flaws in ubiquitous web server software with a demonstrated exploit, but no exploitation in the wild has been reported.
items.detection_coverage_note: This is an assessment: watch for NGINX worker crashes and unusual child processes spawned by NGINX. Patching is the main control.
items.recommended_action: Inventory NGINX instances, including those embedded in appliances and containers, and update them to the fixed releases, starting with internet-facing systems. The Hacker News: Upgrade to NGINX 1.31.9 or 1.30.7. If you cannot patch right away, consider temporarily disabling HTTP/2 on exposed servers. Qualys Vulnerabilities and Threat Research: Find nginx deployments, prioritise internet-facing servers with HTTP/2 enabled, and apply the F5 patches.

items.headline: NGINX HTTP/2 proxy use-after-free enables denial of service and possible code execution (CVE-2026-123633)
items.summary: CVE-2026-123633 affects NGINX Plus and NGINX Open Source when they use HTTP/2 for client connections and proxy requests to a backend. A crafted request can trigger a use-after-free in a worker process that is running low on worker_connections. This causes denial of service, and code execution is possible if ASLR is disabled or can be bypassed. No exploitation has been reported in the source.
items.importance_rationale: This is a remote memory-corruption flaw with possible code execution in globally deployed web server software, but no exploitation has been reported.

items.headline: NGINX proxy use-after-free with SSI or mirror subrequests may allow RCE
items.summary: The flaw affects NGINX proxy setups whose proxied server name uses variables, combined with SSI or mirror subrequests. items.importance_rationale: Possible RCE in widely deployed NGINX, but it needs a specific configuration and an ASLR bypass. No exploitation or CVSS score is reported.
items.detection_coverage_note: Assessment: repeated worker crashes or segfaults in NGINX logs could point to exploitation attempts.
items.recommended_action: Review configs for variable proxy_pass targets combined with SSI or mirror directives, and patch those instances first. Make sure ASLR is enabled.
items.model_importance_rationale: Possible RCE in widely deployed NGINX, but it needs a specific configuration and an ASLR bypass. No exploitation or CVSS score is reported.
